facts.raw_span: A woman in her 60s presented with a 3-month history of pain, swelling, and erythema on her face
left breast carcinoma diagnosed eleven years earlier
treated with mastectomy, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy
left supraclavicular lymph nodes metastasis treated with surgical excision
pain on palpation
no fever or chills
Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek, predominantly involving the left side of the face
Hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and dilated vessels in the dermis
nests of highly atypical cells
Epithelial cells in the dilated vessels were positive for CD31
atypical cells were strongly positive for GATA3
Telangiectatic, swelling erythema mainly involving the left side of the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek

concepts.why: The patient has a history of breast carcinoma and presents with violaceous swelling and telangiectasia on the face, which is consistent with cutaneous metastasis, and the presence of atypical cells positive for GATA3 supports this diagnosis.
The patient presents with telangiectasia and necrosis on the face, and the histopathological examination shows dilated vessels with atypical cells, which is consistent with angiosarcoma of the skin.

The patient presents with violaceous swelling and telangiectasia on the face, which could be consistent with basal cell carcinoma, although the presence of atypical cells positive for GATA3 makes cutaneous metastasis of breast carcinoma more likely.

The patient presents with violaceous swelling and telangiectasia on the face, which could be consistent with squamous cell carcinoma, although the presence of atypical cells positive for GATA3 makes cutaneous metastasis of breast carcinoma more likely.

The patient presents with telangiectasia and necrosis on the face, which could be consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma, although the presence of atypical cells positive for GATA3 makes cutaneous metastasis of breast carcinoma more likely.

The patient presents with violaceous swelling and telangiectasia on the face, which could be consistent with Merkel cell carcinoma, although the presence of atypical cells positive for GATA3 makes cutaneous metastasis of breast carcinoma more likely.

The patient presents with telangiectasia and necrosis on the face, which could be consistent with lymphangiosarcoma, although the presence of atypical cells positive for GATA3 makes cutaneous metastasis of breast carcinoma more likely.

The patient presents with violaceous swelling and telangiectasia on the face, which could be consistent with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, although the presence of atypical cells positive for GATA3 makes cutaneous metastasis of breast carcinoma more likely.

rationales.F02: History of breast carcinoma increases the likelihood of cutaneous metastasis.
rationales.F04: Previous metastasis to lymph nodes increases the likelihood of cutaneous metastasis.
rationales.F07: Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis is suggestive of cutaneous metastasis or angiosarcoma.
rationales.F09: Presence of highly atypical cells is indicative of malignancy.
rationales.F10: CD31 positivity is consistent with vascular tumors such as cutaneous metastasis or angiosarcoma.
rationales.F11: GATA3 positivity is highly suggestive of breast carcinoma metastasis, ruling out other vascular tumors.
